body:
I'm running completion module successfully. However, if I am editing a filetype that has servers but where those servers do not have completion, I keep getting this message:

> method textDocument/completion is not supported by any of the servers registered for the current buffer

This is correct, but how do I silence this? 

For example: when I'm editing a fish shell script with null-ls for formatting, I know I don't have completion. This makes it almost impossible to edit the script as it pop-up frequently.

reply_data.body:
Aha, thanks to this I was able to reproduce. The reason this doesn't happen in my setup is because I manually set function on attach of every LSP server that happen to have completion capability. This shouldn't be the case and I'll try to fix this tomorrow.

In the meantime here is what should work as (temporary or permanent) solution:
- Use this 'mini.completion' setup:
```lua
require('mini.completion').setup({
  lsp_completion = { source_func = 'omnifunc', auto_setup = false },
})
```
- Manually set appropriate omnifunc on attach every server you would like to have completion. [Here](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/487ce206d88412db5577435ba956fcf5a19d6302/lua/ec/configs/nvim-lspconfig.lua#L11-L26) is how I do it (with [this usage](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/487ce206d88412db5577435ba956fcf5a19d6302/lua/ec/configs/nvim-lspconfig.lua#L53)). I generally [recommend this approach](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/93e0f4b2e886813c65c94c5071f08cac6aacaed1/lua/mini/completion.lua#L62-L68).

reply_data.body:
So, as far as I can tell, this output (and the one I have as well) tells that this particular LSP server *should* support completion, because there is a non-`nil` `server_capabilities.completionProvider` element. Here is the [source](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/14090#issuecomment-1113956767) of supposedly canonical way of checking if this. The `completionProvider` is checked for `textDocument/completion` based on [this table entry](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/09c6ce8c4e4c6415cca9b834539ed0df461373f6/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L58) from Neovim core.

So I am not sure what to do here, as at the moment it *feels* like an issue with 'null-ls', but it might as well be its intended behavior.
